primary_sources.title: Finite temperature effective action, AdS5 black holes, and 1/N expansion
locators: section 2 eqs. (2.1)-(2.6): T0, T1, classical action, SBH negative mode and determinant prefactors
section 3 eqs. (3.3)-(3.5): microscopic Seff unavailable at finite/large lambda and phenomenological truncation
section 4 eqs. (4.33)-(4.41): finite-N two-saddle sum, Gaussian factors, O(N^-2) crossover scale
section 5 eqs. (5.1)-(5.4): tunnelling rates and Gaussian prefactors; equilibrium flow balance
primary_sources.role: classical black-hole saddles, Euclidean bounce rates, phenomenological Polyakov-loop matrix model, finite-N two-saddle crossover
source_notes: AGGL section 2 quotes T2 only parametrically as (R*l_p^4)^(-1/5); it does not provide the conditional 0.430 coefficient proposed from the KK gas.
AGGL K_i are Gaussian factors of their phenomenological matrix integral; do not equate them automatically with complete gravitational one-loop determinants.

primary_sources.title: Spectrum of Large N Gauge Theory from Supergravity
locators: text immediately following eq. (2.1): integer bosonic and half-odd-integer fermionic global-AdS energies; singleton exception
primary_sources.role: polynomial KK one-particle density rho(epsilon)~epsilon^8 and thermal gas entropy scaling
source_notes: HO establishes the asymptotic power, not the D=256 coefficient proposed by the neighbor.
The cumulative single-particle count is proportional to epsilon^9 if rho_1(epsilon) is the fixed-energy-level density epsilon^8.

source_corrections: Do not attribute the AdS5-Schwarzschild thermodynamic formulae to Yaffe without a precise verified source; cite Hawking-Page and Witten.
AGGL call their matrix model phenomenological and explicitly note that finite/strong-coupling microscopic effective-action coefficients are unavailable in their treatment.
The KK gas partition and the stringy Hagedorn sector are distinct; the KK gas alone has polynomial one-particle growth.
